title: The productivity extension — question explanation
learningObjective: Evaluate extension permissions, provenance and necessity before installation
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: A browser extension promises to summarize every page. It requests permission to read and change all data on every website, including internal work portals.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Evaluate extension permissions, provenance and necessity before installation
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option C: Check organizational approval, publisher provenance, necessity and permission scope before installation. Broad access to every site creates significant data and account exposure and should be justified and approved.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option A: Using another person’s profile does not resolve the extension’s access or policy risks. Option B: Private mode does not necessarily prevent an extension from accessing permitted page content. Option D: Ratings do not establish the publisher’s trustworthiness or justify broad permissions.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Do not install until the extension is approved and its permissions are proportionate to a documented need. An extension with broad permissions can access sensitive page data; assess source and scope before use.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.
scenes.onScreenText: An extension with broad permissions can access sensitive page data; assess source and scope before use.

narration: Scenario: A browser extension promises to summarize every page. It requests permission to read and change all data on every website, including internal work portals. Safest response: Option C: Check organizational approval, publisher provenance, necessity and permission scope before installation. Broad access to every site creates significant data and account exposure and should be justified and approved. Option A is unsafe because Using another person’s profile does not resolve the extension’s access or policy risks. Option B is unsafe because Private mode does not necessarily prevent an extension from accessing permitted page content. Option D is unsafe because Ratings do not establish the publisher’s trustworthiness or justify broad permissions. In practice: Do not install until the extension is approved and its permissions are proportionate to a documented need. Key takeaway: An extension with broad permissions can access sensitive page data; assess source and scope before use.
